provenance.citation: Boden, M. A. (1977). Artificial Intelligence and Natural Man. New York: Basic Books. Chapter 6: "Programs That Model the Mind." [Conflict detection framework: neurosis as simultaneous maintenance of mutually incompatible beliefs, pp. 198–212.]
provenance.locus: Chapter 6, pp. 198–212 — conflict detection framework; worked example of "impossible double binding" where an agent holds p and ¬p simultaneously across distinct inference paths.
provenance.notes: Boden (1977) is a monograph with no online PDF; the paper_path is citation-only. The conflict detection framework (Chapter 6) is the theoretical foundation: neurosis in an AI system corresponds to maintaining beliefs B and ¬B simultaneously across separate reasoning paths, each locally coherent but globally inconsistent. The six belief pairs here are adapted to the deployment/operations domain: (1) redundancy vs. SPOF, (2) full automation vs. mandatory manual gate, (3) ephemeral containers vs. local disk writes, (4) horizontal stateless scaling vs. single-writer database, (5) immutable config image vs. live runtime flag updates, (6) complete observability vs. 1%-sampled tracing. Each pair is a structurally valid Boden-style double-bind: the agent's inference engine would reach contradictory conclusions depending on which belief it activates first. The existing realAutoinstinctNeurosisInput fixture in breed-inputs-real.ts uses scalar belief strengths (0.0–1.0) rather than semantic contradiction pairs; this canonical example uses the richer string-valued fact encoding to capture the propositional content of each contradictory belief, making the conflict detectable without numeric thresholding.

input.intent: detect contradictory operational beliefs in a distributed deployment agent

facts.value: high — multiple replicas ensure no single point of failure
low — any single node outage causes full service loss
true — CI/CD pipeline handles all releases without human review
true — all production changes require sign-off from on-call engineer
true — containers are stateless; no durable data written locally
true — latency constraints require in-process data cache written to local disk
true — load is distributed across N identical stateless pods
true — all writes funnel through one primary to preserve ordering guarantees
true — service config baked into container image at build time
true — feature flags and thresholds updated live via config service without redeploy
true — every operation emits a span; no blind spots
true — only 1% of traces are retained to control storage costs

expected.description: Boden's conflict detection framework predicts the system identifies each mutually incompatible belief pair as a neurotic double-bind. The agent simultaneously affirms p and ¬p across six operational dimensions. A conforming neurosis breed must surface at minimum one finding per contradiction pair and report status='has_findings'.
